cases.doc:
Also raised when the oracle *is* fresh but returns a non-positive reference value --
freshness and positivity are independent properties, and this contract must not trust
the latter blindly (defense-in-depth against a buggy/compromised oracle; found during
an audit review).
cases.name: OracleStale

fields.doc: SY shares withheld as the tokenization fee.
fields.name: fee_shares

function_v0.doc:
Permissionless keeper call: extend this contract's *instance* storage (admin, config,
reserves, totals, settlement rate, fee buckets) for ~30 days. Soroban does not bump instance
TTL on ordinary reads or writes, so a long-dated market needs this called periodically (or
an archived instance restored) -- see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
function_v0.name: bump

function_v0.doc:
Split `sy_shares` into PT + YT. The caller must already hold these shares in the
SYWrapper and must authorize both this call and the resulting SYWrapper transfer. The
tokenization fee is withheld from `sy_shares` before the PT/YT notional is computed.

Returns the PT and YT minted (equal at issuance) and the fee withheld.
function_v0.name: mint

function_v0.doc:
Redeem PT and/or YT after maturity. Both can be supplied in any combination.

* `pt_amount` \xe2\x80\x94 PT tokens to burn (0 = skip PT redemption)
* `yt_amount` \xe2\x80\x94 YT tokens to burn (0 = skip YT redemption)

Burns the caller's real PT/YT balances and releases real underlying via SYWrapper at the
frozen settlement rate. Returns the underlying units actually transferred for each type.
function_v0.name: redeem

function_v0.doc: Read-only counterpart to `set_paused`. Before this existed, a dApp could only infer the\npaused state indirectly, by attempting a call and catching `Error::Paused`.
function_v0.name: is_paused

function_v0.doc: Before maturity: burn `amount` PT and `amount` YT and return `amount * SCALE / rate` SY\nshares at the current oracle rate. Yield the YT already accrued stays claimable.
function_v0.name: recombine

function_v0.doc:
One-time initialization.

* `sy_wrapper`    \xe2\x80\x94 address of the SYWrapper contract
* `pt_token`      \xe2\x80\x94 address of the PTToken contract (this contract must later be
registered as its minter via `PTToken.set_minter`)
* `yt_token`      \xe2\x80\x94 address of the YTToken contract (same two-phase pattern)
* `oracle`        \xe2\x80\x94 address of the OracleAdapter contract
* `permissioning` \xe2\x80\x94 address of the Permissioning contract
* `underlying`    \xe2\x80\x94 address of the underlying asset; `admin` must be its issuer authority
* `maturity`      \xe2\x80\x94 Unix timestamp at which PT and YT can be redeemed
* `market_config` \xe2\x80\x94 the market's MarketConfig (fees and fee split); its underlying and
maturity must match

`admin` must be the underlying's issuer authority (for a SAC: `admin()`, read live) and
must authorize this call -- creating a new market (even a new maturity on an existing
asset) requires the issuer's participation, matching `SYWrapper`'s market-creation gate.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc:
Freeze the market's settlement rate. Permissionless; callable once the market has matured
and the oracle is fresh. Advances (and thereby freezes) `YTToken`'s index and records its
final rate as the rate every redemption uses. Idempotent: later calls return the recorded
rate.
function_v0.name: settle_all

function_v0.doc:
Claim accrued YT yield without redeeming (burning) the underlying YT position. Available
before maturity -- continuous accrual is the point of holding YT ahead of redemption --
unlike `redeem`, this does not require the market to have matured. The YT fee is deducted
from the payout. Returns the underlying paid to `from`.
function_v0.name: claim_yield

function_v0.doc: SY shares accrued but not yet claimed: (protocol, creator).
function_v0.name: accrued_fees

function_v0.doc: The frozen settlement rate, once `settle_all` (or the first redemption) has run.
function_v0.name: settled_rate

function_v0.doc:
Wire the RiskControl this market reports mints to. This contract must also be registered
as a consumer on that RiskControl or every mint reverts.

Unlike `set_recovery_escrow`-style setters elsewhere, this is updatable (no "already set"
guard), so a wrong address here is not irreversible the same way -- but an admin mistake
(e.g. a copy-pasted address of some other contract entirely) would otherwise only surface
the next time a user mints. This calls back into the given address's own `is_consumer` --
the one read-only view every real RiskControl exposes -- so a non-RiskControl address
(wrong contract type, unrelated address) fails this call instead of silently being wired
in. Deliberately does not require the *result* to be `true`: every deployment path in
this repo (see `scripts/create_market.sh`, `MarketFactory`) calls `set_risk_control`
before the matching `RiskControl.add_consumer`, so this contract is not registered yet at
this point.
function_v0.name: set_risk_control

function_v0.doc: Pay the market creator's accrued share, in SY shares, to the creator (the underlying's\ncurrent issuer authority). Permissionless. Returns the shares paid.
function_v0.name: claim_creator_fees

function_v0.doc: Pay Principal's accrued share of the market's fees, in SY shares, to the config's\ntreasury. Permissionless -- the payee is fixed by configuration. Returns the shares paid.
function_v0.name: claim_protocol_fees
